chapter: South America and back in New York
title: A year of Loew's vaudeville and inspiring Jimmie Lunceford
summary: Lyons books the band for Loew's vaudeville, and in Buffalo the young Lunceford band studies their glee-club number.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So now I was taken away from the piano. But we started -- Lyons said, 'Well, now we're going to do vaude-'

-ville, which we did. Being a Loew -- he was the Loew agent. So, naturally, the whole year that we were back, we did that. From Loew's, from place to place, place to place, we'd play and play and we'd come back to Loew's State about four times. We'd already played it once out of the Club Alabam. But, here's the point that followed us now was on account of being like that, why we couldn't, we didn't play any more dances, see? We was just playing vaudeville. We had one date that was worth mentioning. We played the Great Lakes Theater in Buffalo and then in that theater we were the inspiring attribute to Jimmy Lunsford's young band at that time. Jimmy had these boys in to the theater every first show. And they sat on the first two rows like he had ordered that, see. They took a lot of our method of playing and all like that, because they felt that we had something. In fact we had a, what do you call, a number there that -- well, more like a glee club. And then, where all the boys came out except the piano and drum and bass. And then we did a -- like a glee club. Well, nobody payed much attention to what we were doing, but it was a big number. Some years later, Jimmy Lunsford come up and get credit for being the band that do with the glee club. And I talked with Jimmy when I had a choir and Jimmy told me in front of all the boys, all the people in the choir, he said, "You know, Sam, you was my inspiration." And I said, "Yes, and you stole my trick, too."
